raw:
Both modules look nearly identical in structure. The checks below are on whether the high-risk system definition is the same in both.

Module A defines 3 points × 4 areas = 12 clauses. Module B's clauses are:
- (7, border), (6, migration), (1, asylum), (6, asylum), (6, border), (1, migration), (7, law), (6, law), (7, migration), (1, border), (1, law), (7, asylum).

That is 12 clauses covering all combinations, so the definitions are the same.

The includes_information clauses are the same four in both modules. The access rules are the same, and the registration rule is the same.

Sentence 1: both capture the system definition and the secure-section rule, so both are full or partial. "Shall include only" is represented as a generic includes predicate in both. I rate both partial, since the "only" and the Article 49 specifics are loosely handled. They agree.

Sentences 2–5: each is covered by one includes clause in both modules, so both are partial or full. The info predicates are bare, so I rate both full for the item. Both are the same, so they agree.

Sentence 6: both have the Commission and authority access rules, so they agree.

The only differences are in naming.
